page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 64 GB of system memory. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture, the server allocates 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. This configuration provides a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 25% at 2678.09. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics generally fall into the average range. For instance, the stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is 10778.72, and uncached large-block memory read bandwidth is 57.86 GB/sec. Multi-threaded decompression tasks show relative weakness, with bzip3 multi-threaded decompression scoring in the bottom 25% at 34.57 GB/sec. Similarly, medium-model LLM prompt processing is limited to 16.86 tokens/sec.

The n2d-highmem-8 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring substantial memory capacity without demanding extreme multi-core compute scaling. It is suited for memory-intensive applications such as database caching, medium-sized Redis deployments, and memory-bound enterprise applications. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which should be factored into architectural planning.
